strategic_issues: Sheikh Hasina's continued presence in India since fleeing Dhaka on 5 August 2024
Bangladesh's post-2024 tilt toward China and Pakistan under the Yunus interim government
Jamaat-e-Islami's election gains concentrated near the India border
trade_dependencies: Bangladesh is one of India's larger regional trading partners
India sent approximately 45,000 tons of emergency diesel to Bangladesh in April 2026 amid fuel shortages (per The Diplomat, Aug 2026)

energy_relationship.notes: India has provided emergency fuel supplies; broader energy cooperation exists but is not the primary friction point

military_relationship.posture: no direct military tension, but India has expressed concern over Bangladesh-Pakistan military normalization
military_relationship.notes: Under the Yunus interim government, Bangladesh resumed direct trade links and direct flights with Pakistan after 14 years, and initiated high-level military-to-military dialogue, including talks on possible Bangladeshi procurement of Pakistan's JF-17 fighter aircraft (Jan 2026, per The Diplomat).

diplomatic_relationship.notes: PM Tarique Rahman (BNP, sworn in Feb 2026) chose China for his first overseas state visit rather than India, elevating ties to a 'China-Bangladesh Community with a Shared Future' (June 2026) and reportedly proposing a China-Myanmar-Bangladesh connectivity corridor. India appointed a cabinet-rank High Commissioner (Dinesh Trivedi, June 2026) and invited Rahman to the Sept 2026 BRICS summit in Delhi; as of the latest reporting Rahman had not yet accepted. A New Delhi press event by Sheikh Hasina on 5 Aug 2026 (the anniversary of her ouster) drew formal Bangladeshi 'outrage', which India said it was not responsible for.

major_disputes: Sheikh Hasina extradition request (Bangladesh has requested her return to face charges related to the 2024 crackdown on protesters; India has not extradited her)
Mangla Port operational agreement reportedly transferred to a Chinese operator, which Indian commentary frames as a strategic concern
Framing disputes over Hasina's public statements from Indian soil
areas_of_cooperation: Continued bilateral trade despite political tension
escalation_factors: Further Bangladesh-Pakistan military cooperation (e.g. potential JF-17 acquisition)
Continued Bangladesh-China infrastructure and connectivity deals seen by India as encroaching on its sphere of influence
Jamaat-e-Islami's growing influence in India-border constituencies
deescalation_factors: India's diplomatic outreach (cabinet-rank envoy, BRICS invitation, emergency fuel aid)
Bangladesh's continued economic dependence on Indian trade
Congratulatory exchanges between Modi and Rahman after the Feb 2026 election

_meta.source: The Diplomat (Aug 2026, two articles); RSIS Commentary (2026); Al Jazeera (Feb 2026); Organiser (Aug 2026); Deccan Herald; Malay Mail (April 2025)
_meta.confidence: moderate-high for the factual sequence of events; commentary framing (e.g. characterizing Bangladesh's foreign policy as 'anti-India') reflects predominantly Indian-aligned sources and should be weighed against Bangladeshi government statements, which describe their approach as seeking 'equity and fairness'
